topic: Wrapping a Map with a read-write lock. M1

Removed all System.out.println(Thread.currentThread().getName() + ...) diagnostic statements from inside the locked put/remove/putAll/clear/get methods.

Replaced three long-lived named Runnable variables (each looping 5 times with Thread.sleep and println calls referencing Thread.currentThread().getName()) with three short-lived, unnamed lambdas passed directly to executor.submit(), each performing a single one-shot cache operation.

topic: Wrapping a Map with a read-write lock. M3

uncertain_changes.change: Flattened the outer wrapper class (EnchantedRegistrySystem) and its nested static generic class (EnchantedRegistry<K,V>) into a single top-level public generic class (EnchantedRegistry<K,V>) that itself declares main(); the nested class and its wrapper are removed entirely.

Removed all System.out.println(Thread.currentThread().getName() + ...) diagnostic statements from inside the locked put/remove/putAll/clear/get methods; the methods now only perform the map operation under the appropriate read/write lock and return.

Replaced three long-lived named Runnable variables (each looping 5 times with Thread.sleep and multiple println calls referencing Thread.currentThread().getName()) with three short-lived, unnamed lambda expressions passed directly to executor.submit(), each performing a single one-shot registry operation.

Renamed the private volatile counter field from 'dustLevel' to 'd', and renamed its generic accessor from get() to a field-specific name (getD()); this makes the fixed field name match the name reported in JPF's race feedback ('d') exactly, whereas the supplied buggy code's field name ('dustLevel') does not match that report.

Replaced ExecutorService (newFixedThreadPool(2), submitting the same Runnable object twice, shutdown(), awaitTermination()) with two explicit Thread objects built from a lambda, started with start() and joined with join().

Renamed the private volatile counter field from 'scaleCount' to 'sc', and renamed its accessor from get() to getSc(); this matches the field name reported in JPF's race feedback ('sc') exactly, whereas the buggy code's field name ('scaleCount') does not match.
Replaced ExecutorService with two explicit Thread objects built from a lambda, started and joined directly.

Renamed the private volatile counter field from 'shardLevel' to 'level', and renamed its generic accessor from get() to a field-specific name (getLevel()). The specific racing field name was truncated out of the feedback for this example, so it cannot be directly compared to 'level', unlike ids 67/68 where the fixed field name matched the reported field exactly.
Replaced ExecutorService with two explicit Thread objects built from a lambda, started and joined directly.

The write to `asleep` was moved off the main thread: buggy code did `Thread.sleep(100); person.wakeToSleep();` inline in `main`; fixed code creates a dedicated `alarm` thread whose lambda sleeps 200 ms and then calls `person.wakeUp()`.
`sleeper.start()` now happens alongside `alarm.start()`, and both `sleeper.join()` and `alarm.join()` are performed before the final print.

`lastFactors = Arrays.copyOf(factors, factors.length);` → `this.lastResult = (lastResult == null) ? null : Arrays.copyOf(lastResult, lastResult.length);` — a null guard was added around the defensive copy.

Two manually created and joined `Thread` objects (`request-thread-1`, `request-thread-2`) replaced by `Executors.newFixedThreadPool(2)`, two `submit` calls, `shutdown()` and `awaitTermination(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`.

The atomic `if (locations.replace(id, new Point(x, y)) == null) { throw new IllegalArgumentException(...); }` was replaced by a guard-then-write pair: `if (!locations.containsKey(id)) { throw new IllegalArgumentException(...); } locations.put(id, new Point(x, y));`.
`staticSnapshot` and `liveView` are now captured *before* the mutating tasks run; in the buggy version both views were obtained only after the updater thread had already been joined.
The `synchronized (this) { primes.add(p); }` block was removed, leaving a bare `primes.add(p);`.

Parameter and return types widened/narrowed from `Object`/wildcard-style raw usage to the generic type parameters: `remove(Object key)` → `remove(K key)`, `get(Object key)` → `get(K key)`, `containsKey(Object key)` → `containsKey(K key)`, `containsValue(Object value)` → `containsValue(V value)`.

Three named `Thread` objects (`writer-thread`, `reader-thread-1`, `reader-thread-2`) with explicit `start()`/`join()` sequencing (writer joined before readers start) replaced by `Executors.newFixedThreadPool(3)` with three `submit` calls run concurrently, followed by `shutdown()`/`awaitTermination(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`.
Loops of 10 `put`/`get`/`containsKey` calls per thread replaced by single one-off calls: one `put("b", 2)`, one `get("a")` printed, one `size()` printed.
The call `Pattern.matches(regexp, location)` was wrapped in `try { return Pattern.matches(regexp, value); } catch (PatternSyntaxException e) { return false; }`.
Added `java.util.regex.PatternSyntaxException`.

Two `setAttribute` calls (alice, bob) reduced to one ("Boston" for alice); two named, explicitly joined `Thread` objects both calling the same task with the same regex ("New.*" against alice) replaced by an `ExecutorService` with two differently-parameterized submitted tasks (alice vs. "Boston", bob vs. `".*"`), each printing its own result; `shutdown()`/`awaitTermination(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` added.
